localBiteReport: The most current on-the-ground report (week of Oct 23–29, 2026) from Captain Blake Nelson of Last Cast Charters, as covered by Great Days Outdoors, puts the Choctawhatchee Bay redfish bite in solid shape post-Hurricane Isaias: smaller slot reds (roughly 23 inches and under) are still holding in the familiar guts, potholes, and shallow feeding areas on the flats, with sight-fishing remaining viable because the bay stayed relatively clear — tannin-stained but never heavily muddy after the storm. Larger upper-slot and oversize bull reds are beginning a more mobile fall transition but haven't fully left the flats yet, and cut mullet on Carolina rigs has been outperforming live bait following recent cold fronts. A guide posting on Captain Experiences (approximately 2 weeks prior, so treat as supporting context rather than breaking news) noted that redfish and trout were heating up in the bayous. Water temperature at this location is 76°F. October is prime flounder-run season for Choctawhatchee Bay, with fish migrating toward the pass, but no specific flounder catch reports surfaced in this week's verified sources; the same is true for black drum and sheepshead, which typically pick up around bridge structure as water cools further into November.
